RagShortTexts: During the Great Interregnum, dual elections paralyze the HRE, allowing princes to expand.

Variants.Content: The Holy Roman Empire languishes in the Great Interregnum following Hohenstaufen extinction. Richard of Cornwall and Alfonso X of Castile contest the Roman kingship, yet neither exerts effective rule over German lands, allowing territorial princes and free cities to consolidate regional independence.

Without an effective emperor, every duke and count acts as Caesar within his own fortress. The electors gladly accepted bullion from London and Toledo, but none desire a ruler strong enough to discipline them.
Castles sprout along the Rhine like weeds, each housing robber knights who shake down river traffic. Mercenaries swear to whoever pays best, clashing over bridge tolls and border rights.
